newsitem.title: BOSNIA: NATO force sacks American translator in Bosnia.
newsitem.headline: NATO force sacks American translator in Bosnia.

text.p: The NATO-led peace force said on Friday it has sacked an American civilian translator after his nationalist Serb sympathies were revealed in photographs published by a local newspaper.

The Sarajevo newspaper Oslobodjenje published pictures this week depicting the employee, Gordon Bardos, kissing a Bosnian Serb flag and raising his three fingers in a traditional nationalist Serb salute.
"Following an investigation as well as legal advice we determined that this type of behaviour is inappropriate and we cannot allow this to happen," NATO spokesman Major Tony White told reporters.
One of the photographs showed Bardos in an American uniform with his three fingers raised, standing in front of a U.S. "Humvee" armoured vehicle parked by a road sign for Pale, outside Sarajevo.
The NATO-led Stabilisation Force (SFOR) seeks to present itself as an impartial mission keeping the peace among rival Moslem, Croat and Serb communities.
Bardos was hired by NATO at the beginning of 1996 to translate, SFOR spokesmen said.

His last assignment had him working for the voter education department of the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE), as part of NATO support for upcoming local elections in September.
